lines.trans: Katya, you and I are together now.
You fill my life with meaning.
Without you I am not myself.
Without you I am nobody.
And I do not want to be anyone else.
You are my world.
You are my life and my universe.
My dear Katya.
Will you marry me?
What do you think, will she forgive me?
Very cool, she will definitely forgive you.
And we will help you with that.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'we', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: We are almost there already.
We work better than everyone here.

examples.text: Сейчас мы быстро наведём здесь порядок!
examples.trans: Right now we will quickly restore order here!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'with / from', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Strong contractions.
I am with you.
Take more air in.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: You should introduce a new service.
You are simply spying on me.
Oh, you little macaque monkey!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'already', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: We are almost there already.
How do you know? Does it show already?
The workday has already started!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'together', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Катя, мы с тобой уже вместе.
examples.trans: Katya, you and I are together now.

examples.text: С тех пор мы всегда вместе.
examples.trans: Since then we have always been together.
We're together.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'полнять'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'you fill'.

examples.trans: You fill my life with meaning.
You fill my life with meaning!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'my', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Oh my God.

examples.text: Ну что, Витя, теперь ты мой раб.
examples.trans: Well then, Vitya, now you are my servant.
At least give my office back.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'life' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: You fill my life with meaning.

examples.text: Ты моя жизнь и моя вселенная.
examples.trans: You are my life and my universe.
You fill my life with meaning!

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'мысл'). Common masculine noun meaning 'with meaning' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: You fill my life with meaning.
You fill my life with meaning!
What do you mean?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'without', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Without you I am not myself.
Without you I am nobody.
That's no problem.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'I', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I am with you.
My butterfly.
Take more air in.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I must not get nervous right now at all.
I have no idea.
No, nothing.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'nobody', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Никто не будет командовать на моей кухне!
examples.trans: Nobody is going to give orders in my kitchen!

examples.text: Не говори об этом никому, ладно?
examples.trans: Do not tell anyone about this, okay?
But legally you are nobody to her.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Strong contractions.
We are almost there already.
Come on, let's breathe.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'want', paired with 'захотеть'.

examples.text: Они хотели внести изменения в меню.
examples.trans: They wanted to make changes to the menu.
I meant well, understand.
I want coffee.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'be'.

examples.trans: And what should I do?
And I do not want to be anyone else.
I have a toy car.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'world' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: You are my world.
You are my world!
Now there's peace.

meanings.note: Prefix 'вс-' ('up') marks upward or sudden onset of action (stem 'еленная'). Common feminine noun meaning 'universe' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Ты моя жизнь и моя вселенная.
examples.trans: You are my life and my universe.
This is a universe.
For ideal order in the universe.

meanings.note: Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'рогой'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('dear').

examples.trans: Let's discuss it on the way.
My dear Katya.
These are expensive clothes.

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will you marry / go out', paired with 'выходить'.

related.gloss: not to will you marry (negated infinitive)

examples.text: Он ведёт себя как ревнивый парень.
examples.trans: He behaves like a jealous boyfriend.
Victor Petrovich, there is a new order here.
Will you marry me?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'for', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: The grand opening is tomorrow.
What kind of nonsense is this?
I accept that after breakfast.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'how', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Он ведёт себя как ревнивый парень.
examples.trans: He behaves like a jealous boyfriend.

examples.text: Я как будто в театр сходил.
examples.trans: It is as if I went to the theater.
And how should I react?

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'think', paired with 'подумать'.

examples.trans: Sorry, I thought the wrong thing.
What do you think, will she forgive me?
I'm thinking about work.

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'стить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'she will forgive', paired with 'прощать'.

related.gloss: not to she will forgive (negated infinitive)

examples.trans: Excuse me, what exactly am I ignoring?
What do you think, will she forgive me?
Very cool, she will definitely forgive you.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'she', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Она нашла нас на новом месте.
examples.trans: She found us at the new place.
That is it, she got really offended.
She is not answering her phone.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'very', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: You two argue really coolly.
Why is there a meat shortage here?
In short, he knows what it is for.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: You two argue really coolly.
Very cool, she will definitely forgive you.
It is the weekend today, everything is cool!

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: But there is definitely one solution.
Very cool, she will definitely forgive you.
Lyolya will definitely come!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and, but', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Strong contractions.
My butterfly.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'in, into', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Strong contractions.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'this', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: What kind of nonsense is this?
This is a service for our guests.
This does not interrupt your rest.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'мочь'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will help', paired with 'помогать'.

examples.text: Вы не волнуйтесь, мы вам поможем!
examples.trans: Do not worry, we will help you!

examples.text: А мы тебе в этом поможем.
examples.trans: And we will help you with that.
Maybe you could help?

meanings.note: Prefix 'об-' ('around, about') marks encirclement or comprehensive action (stem 'ращать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to turn, to direct', paired with 'обратить'.

examples.trans: Pay attention to the balcony above.
Do not pay attention.

meanings.note: Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'attention' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Pay attention to the balcony above.
May I have your attention.
Thank you for your attention.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'верх').

examples.text: Сейчас мы быстро наведём здесь порядок!
examples.trans: Right now we will quickly restore order here!
Pay attention to the balcony above.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'егодня').

examples.trans: Today we have a draw.
Did they bring the mussels today? No.
I will fire all of you today!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'in the evening', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Сегодня вечером я сделаю ей предложение!
examples.trans: Tonight I will propose to her!
Thank you for a wonderful evening, Vitya!
Come in the evening.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'делать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will do', paired with 'делать'.

examples.trans: Please make coffee for the tables.

examples.text: Михаил сделает нам туалет, как просим.
examples.trans: Mikhail will give us a restroom as we ask.

examples.text: Сегодня вечером я сделаю ей предложение!
examples.trans: Tonight I will propose to her!

meanings.note: Prefix 'пред-' ('before, fore-') indicates anticipation or prior position (stem 'ложение'). Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'offer, proposal; sentence' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Сегодня вечером я сделаю ей предложение!
examples.trans: Tonight I will propose to her!
It's a good offer, of course.
I have a proposal.
